gaps.lead: I can't wait for the holidays to start.
gaps.explanation: look forward TO + -ing: the 'to' is a preposition.

gaps.lead: Someone must check this equipment before every flight.
gaps.explanation: must check → must be checked (modal + be + past participle).

gaps.lead: He didn't study, so he failed the exam.
gaps.sentence: If he had studied, he ___ the exam.
gaps.explanation: If + past perfect, would have + past participle.

gaps.lead: If I were in charge, overtime would be paid automatically.
gaps.explanation: Dropping 'if' inverts the subjunctive: Were I in charge…

gaps.lead: The film we saw last week was better than this one.
gaps.sentence: This film is not ___ the one we saw last week.
gaps.explanation: 'Not as good as' expresses an inferior comparison.

gaps.lead: Someone stole her bike last week.
gaps.explanation: have something stolen/done = experience it happening to you.

gaps.lead: He began playing chess at the age of six.
gaps.sentence: He ___ at the age of six.
gaps.explanation: take up = start (a hobby or sport): took up chess.

gaps.lead: 'Have you seen my keys anywhere?' he asked us.
gaps.sentence: He asked us ___ his keys anywhere.
gaps.explanation: if/whether + subject + backshifted verb: whether we had seen.
